name: Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom
description: Classification systems, algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms

cards.term: Which organisms, once placed in Plantae, have now been excluded from it?
cards.definition: Fungi, and members of Monera and Protista having cell walls

cards.term: Why are cyanobacteria (blue green algae) no longer called 'algae'?
cards.definition: They are prokaryotes (Monera), now excluded from Plantae

cards.term: Which five groups does NCERT describe under Plantae?
cards.definition: Algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms, angiosperms

cards.term: What characters did the earliest (artificial) classification systems use?
cards.definition: Gross superficial morphological characters: habit, colour, number and shape of leaves, etc.

cards.term: On which structure was Linnaeus' artificial system mainly based?
cards.definition: The androecium (and vegetative characters)

cards.term: Give two drawbacks of artificial systems.
cards.definition:
• They separated closely related species, being based on a few characters
  • They gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characters, though vegetative characters are more easily affected by environment

cards.term: On what are natural classification systems based?
cards.definition: Natural affinities: external and internal features such as ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology and phytochemistry

cards.term: Who gave a natural classification for flowering plants?
cards.definition: George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker

cards.term: On what are phylogenetic classification systems based?
cards.definition: Evolutionary relationships; organisms of the same taxa are assumed to have a common ancestor

cards.term: What is numerical taxonomy?
cards.definition: Classification using all observable characters, coded as numbers and processed by computer; each character gets equal importance

cards.term: What is cytotaxonomy based on?
cards.definition: Cytological information: chromosome number, structure and behaviour

cards.term: What does chemotaxonomy use?
cards.definition: The chemical constituents of the plant

cards.term: Describe algae in five words (NCERT).
cards.definition: Chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, largely aquatic

cards.term: Name three non-aquatic habitats of algae.
cards.definition: Moist stones, soils and wood

cards.term: Algae live in association with which organisms?
cards.definition: Fungi (lichen) and animals (e.g. on sloth bear)

cards.text: Algae range from colonial forms like {{c1::Volvox}} to filamentous forms like {{c2::Ulothrix and Spirogyra}}; marine {{c3::kelps}} form massive plant bodies.

cards.term: How do algae reproduce vegetatively?
cards.definition: By fragmentation; each fragment develops into a thallus

cards.term: What are the most common asexual spores of algae?
cards.definition: Zoospores: flagellated (motile), germinating into new plants

cards.term: Isogamy, anisogamy and oogamy in algae
cards.definition: Isogamy: similar gametes, flagellated (Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (Spirogyra). Anisogamy: dissimilar in size (Eudorina). Oogamy: large non-motile egg + small motile male (Volvox, Fucus).

cards.term: What is isogamy?
cards.definition: Fusion of two gametes similar in size, flagellated (Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (Spirogyra)

cards.term: What is anisogamy? Example?
cards.definition: Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, e.g. Eudorina

cards.term: What is oogamy? Examples?
cards.definition: Fusion of a large, non-motile (static) female gamete with a smaller, motile male gamete, e.g. Volvox, Fucus

cards.term: Figure 3.1 · Name each alga
Figure 3.1 · Volvox
Figure 3.1 · Laminaria
Figure 3.1 · Fucus
How much of the total CO<sub>2</sub> fixation on earth do algae carry out?
cards.definition: At least half

cards.term: Why are algae of paramount importance in water?
cards.definition: As primary producers of energy-rich compounds, the basis of aquatic food cycles; they also raise dissolved oxygen

cards.term: How many species of marine algae are used as food? Name three genera.
cards.definition: About 70: Porphyra, Laminaria, Sargassum

cards.text: Hydrocolloids: {{c1::algin}} comes from brown algae and {{c2::carrageen}} from red algae.

cards.term: What are hydrocolloids?
cards.definition: Water holding substances, used commercially

cards.term: Agar is obtained from which algae?
cards.definition: Gelidium and Gracilaria

cards.term: What is agar used for?
cards.definition: Growing microbes, and in ice-creams and jellies

cards.term: Which unicellular alga is used as a protein-rich food supplement, even by space travellers?
cards.definition: Chlorella

cards.term: Name the three main classes of algae.
cards.definition: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, Rhodophyceae

cards.term: What is the basis of classifying algae into classes?
cards.definition: The type of pigment and the type of stored food

cards.term: What is the common name of Chlorophyceae?
cards.definition: Green algae

cards.term: Why are green algae grass green?
cards.definition: Dominance of chlorophyll a and b

cards.term: Name six shapes of chloroplasts in green algae.
cards.definition: Discoid, plate-like, reticulate, cup-shaped, spiral, ribbon-shaped

cards.term: What are pyrenoids, and what do they contain?
cards.definition: Storage bodies in the chloroplasts; they contain protein besides starch

cards.term: Besides starch, in what form may some green algae store food?
cards.definition: Oil droplets

cards.term: What is the cell wall of green algae made of?
cards.definition: Inner layer of cellulose, outer layer of pectose

cards.term: Where are zoospores produced in green algae?
cards.definition: In zoosporangia

cards.term: Name five common green algae.
cards.definition: Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra, Chara

cards.term: Where are brown algae found?
cards.definition: Primarily in marine habitats

cards.term: Give a simple and a profusely branched brown alga.
cards.definition: Simple branched filamentous: Ectocarpus. Profusely branched: kelps

cards.term: How tall may kelps grow?
cards.definition: 100 metres

cards.term: Which pigments do brown algae possess?
cards.definition: Chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls

cards.term: Which pigment decides the colour (olive green to brown) of brown algae?
cards.definition: The xanthophyll fucoxanthin

cards.term: In what form do brown algae store food?
cards.definition: Complex carbohydrates: laminarin or mannitol

cards.term: What covers the cellulosic wall of brown algae?
cards.definition: A gelatinous coating of algin

cards.text: A brown alga is attached to the substratum by a {{c1::holdfast}}, has a stalk, the {{c2::stipe}}, and a leaf-like photosynthetic organ, the {{c3::frond}}.

cards.term: Describe the zoospores of brown algae.
cards.definition: Biflagellate, pear-shaped, with two unequal laterally attached flagella

cards.term: Where may union of gametes take place in brown algae?
cards.definition: In water, or within the oogonium (oogamous species)

cards.term: Name five common brown algae.
cards.definition: Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum, Fucus

cards.term: Why are red algae red?
cards.definition: Predominance of the red pigment r-phycoerythrin

cards.term: Where are most red algae found?
cards.definition: Marine, with greater concentrations in warmer areas

cards.term: At what depths do red algae occur?
cards.definition: Both near the surface and at great depths where little light penetrates

cards.term: In what form do red algae store food?
cards.definition: Floridean starch, very similar to amylopectin and glycogen

cards.term: How do red algae reproduce asexually and sexually?
cards.definition: Asexually by non-motile spores; sexually by non-motile gametes (oogamous)

cards.term: What follows fertilisation in red algae?
cards.definition: Complex post fertilisation developments

cards.term: Name four common red algae.
cards.definition: Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria, Gelidium

cards.term: Algae classes: pigments
cards.definition: Chlorophyceae: Chlorophyll a, b; Phaeophyceae: Chlorophyll a, c, fucoxanthin; Rhodophyceae: Chlorophyll a, d, phycoerythrin

cards.term: Algae classes: habitat
cards.definition: Chlorophyceae: Fresh water, brackish water, salt water; Phaeophyceae: Fresh water (rare), brackish, salt water; Rhodophyceae: Fresh water (some), brackish, salt water (most)

cards.term: Which class of algae has no flagellated cells?
cards.definition: Rhodophyceae (red algae)

cards.term: Which chlorophyll is found only in red algae (among the three classes)?
cards.definition: Chlorophyll d

cards.term: Which plants make up the bryophytes, and where do they grow?
cards.definition: Mosses and liverworts, in moist shaded areas in the hills

cards.term: Why are bryophytes called the 'amphibians of the plant kingdom'?
cards.definition: They live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction

cards.term: What role do bryophytes play on bare rocks and soil?
cards.definition: An important role in plant succession

cards.term: What attaches a bryophyte to the substratum?
cards.definition: Unicellular or multicellular rhizoids

cards.term: Do bryophytes have true roots, stems or leaves?
cards.definition: No. They may have root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures

cards.term: Is the main plant body of a bryophyte haploid or diploid? What is it called?
cards.definition: Haploid; it produces gametes, so it is the gametophyte

cards.text: The male sex organ of bryophytes, the {{c1::antheridium}}, produces {{c2::biflagellate antherozoids}}; the flask-shaped female sex organ, the {{c3::archegonium}}, produces a {{c4::single egg}}.

cards.term: Are the sex organs of bryophytes unicellular or multicellular?
cards.definition: Multicellular

cards.term: Does the bryophyte zygote undergo meiosis at once?
cards.definition: No. It forms a multicellular sporophyte first

cards.term: Is the bryophyte sporophyte free-living?
cards.definition: No. It is attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it

cards.term: In bryophytes, which cells undergo meiosis and what do they form?
cards.definition: Some cells of the sporophyte, forming haploid spores, which germinate into gametophytes

cards.term: Dominant generation: bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms
cards.definition: Bryophytes: gametophyte dominant, sporophyte dependent on it. Pteridophytes: sporophyte dominant; gametophyte (prothallus) small, free-living. Gymnosperms: sporophyte dominant; gametophytes reduced, not free-living.

cards.term: Which moss provides peat?
cards.definition: Sphagnum

cards.term: What is peat (from Sphagnum) used for?
cards.definition: Fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material (it holds water)

cards.term: Which organisms are the first to colonise rocks?
cards.definition: Mosses along with lichens

cards.term: How do mosses help higher plants on rocks?
cards.definition: They decompose rocks, making the substrate suitable for higher plants

cards.term: How do mosses prevent soil erosion?
cards.definition: Their dense mats reduce the impact of falling rain

cards.term: Into which two groups are bryophytes divided?
cards.definition: Liverworts and mosses

cards.term: Name five habitats of liverworts.
cards.definition: Banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees, deep in the woods

cards.term: Give an example of a thalloid liverwort.
cards.definition: Marchantia

cards.term: Describe the thallus of a liverwort.
cards.definition: Dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate

cards.term: How are the leaf-like appendages of leafy liverworts arranged?
cards.definition: Tiny, in two rows on the stem-like structures

cards.term: What are gemmae?
cards.definition: Green, multicellular, asexual buds that develop in gemma cups on the thalli

cards.term: Where do gemmae develop?
cards.definition: In small receptacles called gemma cups

cards.term: Into what is the liverwort sporophyte differentiated?
cards.definition: Foot, seta and capsule

cards.term: Figure 3.2 · Marchantia: (a) female thallus, (b) male thallus
In Marchantia, which thallus bears the archegoniophore?
cards.definition: The female thallus (the male bears the antheridiophore)

cards.term: Which stage is predominant in the life cycle of a moss?
cards.definition: The gametophyte

cards.term: Name the two stages of the moss gametophyte.
cards.definition: The protonema stage and the leafy stage

cards.term: Describe the protonema.
cards.definition: Develops directly from a spore; creeping, green, branched, frequently filamentous

cards.term: From what does the leafy stage of a moss develop?
cards.definition: From the secondary protonema, as a lateral bud

cards.term: Which stage of the moss bears the sex organs?
cards.definition: The leafy stage

cards.term: How are leaves arranged in the leafy stage of a moss?
cards.definition: Spirally, on upright slender axes

cards.term: What kind of rhizoids do mosses have?
cards.definition: Multicellular and branched

cards.term: How do mosses reproduce vegetatively?
cards.definition: By fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema

cards.term: Where are the sex organs of a moss produced?
cards.definition: At the apex of the leafy shoots

cards.term: Compare the sporophyte of mosses with that of liverworts.
cards.definition: Moss sporophyte (foot, seta, capsule) is more elaborate; mosses have an elaborate spore dispersal mechanism

cards.term: Name three common mosses.
cards.definition: Funaria, Polytrichum, Sphagnum

cards.term: Figure 3.2 (c) · Funaria: gametophyte and sporophyte
Figure 3.2 (d) · Sphagnum gametophyte
Liverworts vs mosses
cards.definition: Plant body: Liverwort: thalloid, dorsiventral. Moss: upright axes with spiral leaves; Asexual: Liverwort: gemmae. Moss: fragmentation, budding in protonema; Sporophyte: Moss: more elaborate (both have foot, seta, capsule)

cards.term: Which plants make up the pteridophytes?
cards.definition: Horsetails and ferns

cards.term: Name three uses of pteridophytes.
cards.definition: Medicinal purposes, soil-binders, ornamentals

cards.term: Which were evolutionarily the first terrestrial plants with vascular tissues?
cards.definition: Pteridophytes (xylem and phloem)

cards.term: Where are pteridophytes found?
cards.definition: Cool, damp, shady places (some in sandy soil)

cards.term: Is the main plant body of a pteridophyte a gametophyte or a sporophyte?
cards.definition: Sporophyte, differentiated into true root, stem and leaves

cards.text: Pteridophyte leaves are small ({{c1::microphylls}}) as in Selaginella, or large ({{c2::macrophylls}}) as in ferns.

cards.term: What are sporophylls?
cards.definition: Leaf-like appendages that subtend the sporangia

cards.term: What are strobili (cones)? Examples?
cards.definition: Compact structures formed by sporophylls, e.g. Selaginella, Equisetum

cards.term: How are spores produced in pteridophytes?
cards.definition: By meiosis in spore mother cells in the sporangia

cards.term: What is the prothallus?
cards.definition: The small, multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte of pteridophytes

cards.term: Why is the spread of living pteridophytes restricted?
cards.definition: The gametophyte needs cool, damp, shady places, and water is needed for fertilisation

cards.term: What is water needed for in pteridophyte fertilisation?
cards.definition: To transfer antherozoids from the antheridia to the mouth of the archegonium

cards.term: What are homosporous pteridophytes?
cards.definition: Those producing similar kinds of spores (the majority)

cards.term: What are heterosporous pteridophytes? Examples?
cards.definition: Those producing macro (large) and micro (small) spores: Selaginella, Salvinia

cards.term: What do megaspores and microspores give rise to?
cards.definition: Megaspores: female gametophytes. Microspores: male gametophytes.

cards.term: Why is heterospory in Selaginella and Salvinia an important step in evolution?
cards.definition: The female gametophyte is retained on the sporophyte and the embryo develops within it: a precursor to the seed habit

cards.term: Pteridophyte classes: examples
cards.definition: Psilopsida: Psilotum; Lycopsida: Selaginella, Lycopodium; Sphenopsida: Equisetum; Pteropsida: Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum

cards.term: Equisetum belongs to which class of pteridophytes?
cards.definition: Sphenopsida (horsetails)

cards.term: Adiantum belongs to which class of pteridophytes?
cards.definition: Pteropsida

Figure 3.3 (a) · Selaginella
Figure 3.3 (b) · Equisetum
What does 'gymnosperm' mean?
cards.definition: Naked seeds (gymnos: naked, sperma: seeds)

cards.term: Why are gymnosperms called naked-seeded?
cards.definition: Ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall before or after fertilisation, so seeds are uncovered

cards.term: Which gymnosperm is one of the tallest tree species?
cards.definition: The giant redwood, Sequoia

cards.term: What kind of roots do gymnosperms generally have?
cards.definition: Tap roots

cards.text: Roots of Pinus have a fungal association called {{c1::mycorrhiza}}; Cycas has small specialised {{c2::coralloid}} roots associated with {{c3::N2-fixing cyanobacteria}}.

cards.term: Give a gymnosperm with an unbranched stem and two with branched stems.
cards.definition: Unbranched: Cycas. Branched: Pinus, Cedrus

cards.term: In which gymnosperm do the pinnate leaves persist for a few years?
cards.definition: Cycas

cards.term: How are conifer leaves adapted to reduce water loss?
cards.definition:
• Needle-like: less surface area
  • Thick cuticle
  • Sunken stomata

cards.term: Are gymnosperms homosporous or heterosporous?
cards.definition: Heterosporous: haploid microspores and megaspores

cards.term: What are male strobili (microsporangiate strobili)?
cards.definition: Strobili bearing microsporophylls and microsporangia

cards.term: What is the pollen grain of a gymnosperm?
cards.definition: The highly reduced male gametophyte, confined to a limited number of cells

cards.term: Where do pollen grains develop?
cards.definition: Within the microsporangia

cards.term: What are female (macrosporangiate) strobili?
cards.definition: Cones bearing megasporophylls with ovules (megasporangia)

cards.term: Are male and female cones on the same tree?
cards.definition: In Pinus, yes. In Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are on different trees.

cards.term: From what is the megaspore mother cell differentiated?
cards.definition: One of the cells of the nucellus

cards.term: What is an ovule?
cards.definition: The nucellus protected by envelopes: a composite structure

cards.term: How many megaspores does the megaspore mother cell form, and how many develop further?
cards.definition: Four by meiosis; one develops into the female gametophyte

cards.term: What does the female gametophyte of a gymnosperm bear?
cards.definition: Two or more archegonia

cards.term: Do gymnosperm gametophytes live independently?
cards.definition: No. Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, they remain within the sporangia on the sporophyte

cards.term: How does the pollen grain reach the ovule in gymnosperms?
cards.definition: Carried by air currents to the opening of the ovules

cards.term: What does the pollen tube do in gymnosperms?
cards.definition: Carries the male gametes towards the archegonia and discharges them near the mouth of the archegonia

cards.term: After fertilisation in gymnosperms, what do the zygote and the ovule become?
cards.definition: Zygote: embryo. Ovule: seed (uncovered).

cards.term: Figure 3.4 · Name each gymnosperm
Figure 3.4 (c) · Ginkgo
Both gymnosperms and angiosperms bear seeds. Why are they classified separately?
cards.definition: Gymnosperm ovules and seeds are naked; angiosperm ovules are in flowers and seeds are enclosed in fruits

cards.term: In angiosperms, where are the pollen grains and ovules developed?
cards.definition: In specialised structures called flowers

cards.term: What encloses the seeds of angiosperms?
cards.definition: Fruits

cards.term: Name the smallest angiosperm and a tall angiosperm tree (with height).
cards.definition: Smallest: Wolffia. Tall: Eucalyptus (over 100 metres)

cards.term: Into which two classes are angiosperms divided?
cards.definition: Dicotyledons and monocotyledons

cards.term: Name four uses of angiosperms.
cards.definition: Food, fodder, fuel, medicines (and other commercial products)

cards.term: Name three groups of plants that bear archegonia.
cards.definition: Bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms

cards.term: Match: Chlamydomonas, Cycas, Selaginella, Sphagnum.
cards.definition: Chlamydomonas: alga. Cycas: gymnosperm. Selaginella: pteridophyte. Sphagnum: moss.

cards.definition: Protonema cell of a moss: n; Leaf cell of a moss: n; Prothallus cell of a fern: n; Gemma cell of Marchantia: n; Zygote of a fern: 2n
